findings.text: assert REMAINING_WARNING_SECONDS == 1800 is agreement with a literal the code itself hard-codes (fleet.py:28 is 30 * 60) rather than a property, so no input can make it fail: it duplicates one design decision in two spellings and cannot tell a wrong threshold from a changed one, which is the shape - an assertion nothing can falsify - that this plan's earlier node shipped at the hold-script wall-clock check. The behaviour it should stand beside is already present in the same test (a 600s fixture warns, a 9000s fixture does not), so the constant equality adds a second reading of the same value rather than a second check.

the state table's heading claims every state is 'covered, over fixture queue text', and its fifth row presents an unreadable token (N/A) as covered with 'remaining unknown, no warning' - but no fixture row carries N/A: the three _fleet_row call sites at tests/agent/test_fleet.py:133, :146 and :157 pass 2:30:00, 0:10:00 and UNLIMITED, and measuring the focused suite's coverage of imas_ambix/agent/fleet.py reports 91% with fleet.py:151 ('remaining = "unknown"') unexecuted, so the rendering and the no-warning half of that state are established by reading the code, not by the suite the record cites - the reader-level assertion remaining_seconds('N/A') is None at tests/agent/test_fleet.py:172 covers only the no-numeric-parse half. The same overstatement appears in the run manifest, whose artifacts line counts five new tests over fixture queue text where the file holds four plus one direct reader test.

the field-count guard accepts 7 or 8 and silently continues on anything else, so a row the scheduler reports in any other shape is dropped before find_fleet_allocation sees it and the command then prints 'no fleet allocation is held' at exit 0 for a queue that holds one - the only path measured here where the absence sentence is produced from a present allocation. It is not reachable on today's queue: the live query this review re-ran (squeue -h -u <user> -A iter with the command's own format) returned 3 rows, every one of them 8 fields, and %k reads (null) for an unset comment so an unrelated row cannot collide with the fleet's token. The leniency is also deliberate: tests/test_agent.py:743 asserts an exact seven-key dict for a seven-field fixture, a path outside this node's write scope, so tightening the guard is a two-file change owned by whoever holds that fixture.

the scheduler-failure path is never exercised through the command this node added: the _squeue fake returns CompletedProcess with returncode 0 unconditionally, so 'query failed' is distinguished from 'nothing held' only at the shared _running_jobs level, where the pre-existing tests/test_agent.py:756 already asserts the raise. The distinction does survive to the command (measured here: returncode 1 yields exit 1 and 'Error: squeue: error: invalid format' with the absence wording absent), but the record's claim that the two are told apart rests on the shared function's test rather than on any test of fleet status.

the gates table quotes the focused suite as '10 passed in 0.64s', which matches neither the run's own fleet-tests.log ('10 passed in 0.69s') nor any other log in the run directory, so the figure is a re-run whose output was not captured rather than a reading of the artifact it cites; the counts match in every case, so this is a traceability gap and not a wrong result.

the three commits this node landed are named in the landing comment's prose at line 414 and in the evidence record, but the machine-readable plan-commits meta does not carry them - at HEAD it lists seven shas and none of them 13acbd20, 8fa8f0ee or 5507cd9f, while the commit that records the destination revision (9ed4ac47) is likewise absent - so a reader of the dashboard, which reads the meta and not the prose, cannot reach this node's implementation commits from the plan.
